TextPage.note: Reading designs the API for reusable text pages; the get_text('dict') and get_text('rawdict') TypedDicts are TextPageDict and RawTextPageDict.

TextPage.poolsize.note: Size of MuPDF's text memory pool; it has no PDF-level meaning.

Shape.note: A context manager that commits on a clean exit. A commit places one Form XObject that embeds each font once; commit() raises for drawing that finish() did not style, and finish() raises for a style that draws nothing, where pymupdf drops or blackens it. The canvas replaces it.

Shape.commit.note: Drawing that finish() did not style raises instead of being dropped.

Shape.draw_cont.note: Raw content buffer of pymupdf's Shape; pylopdf generates content through krilla.

Shape.finish.note: Options are keyword-only; morph= and oc= are not available. A style that would draw nothing, without fill and with color=None or width=0, raises where pymupdf strokes in black.

Shape.height.note: pylopdf's Shape draws in display coordinates, where these values of pymupdf's unrotated space would mix coordinate spaces; shape.page.rect gives the drawing area.

Shape.insert_text.note: Takes Page.insert_text's font options, font= and lineheight= included, splits text, places lines, and leaves out the lines below the page as it does, and returns the line count; fill=, render_mode=, border_width=, miter_limit=, rotate=, morph=, the opacities, and oc= are not available.

Shape.insert_textbox.note: Takes Page.insert_textbox's font and layout options, font= and lineheight= included, and places lines as it does; fill=, render_mode=, border_width=, miter_limit=, rotate=, morph=, the opacities, and oc= are not available.

Shape.ipctm.note: pylopdf's Shape draws in display coordinates, where these values of pymupdf's unrotated space would mix coordinate spaces; shape.page.rect gives the drawing area.

Shape.pctm.note: pylopdf's Shape draws in display coordinates, where these values of pymupdf's unrotated space would mix coordinate spaces; shape.page.rect gives the drawing area.

Shape.text_cont.note: Raw content buffer of pymupdf's Shape; pylopdf generates content through krilla.

Shape.totalcont.note: Raw content buffer of pymupdf's Shape; pylopdf generates content through krilla.

Shape.width.note: pylopdf's Shape draws in display coordinates, where these values of pymupdf's unrotated space would mix coordinate spaces; shape.page.rect gives the drawing area.

Font.note: Standard 14 fonts by name or alias, OpenType files and buffers, and installed font extras through the keyword-only language= and family=; the keyword-only weight= also selects an instance of a variable font file. script=, ordering=, embed=, and pymupdf's other built-in fonts are not available, and is_bold=, is_italic=, and is_serif= raise with fontname or a font file instead of being ignored.

Font.ascender.note: pymupdf's value: what FreeType reads for MuPDF, the OS/2 typographic ascender when the face sets USE_TYPO_METRICS and the hhea ascender otherwise, or the bounding box of MuPDF's URW font for a Standard 14 font; insert_text and insert_textbox place lines with it.

Font.descender.note: pymupdf's value, from the same table as Font.ascender; insert_text and insert_textbox place lines with it.

Font.has_glyph.note: Takes a code point and returns its glyph number, or 0; a one-character string is also accepted, and language=, script=, fallback=, and small_caps= are not available. A Standard 14 font has no glyph numbers, so its number is the character's code in the font's encoding.

Font.is_serif.note: Classified from the PANOSE serif style or the family name, where pymupdf reports every OpenType face as serif.

Font.name.note: The family and style of an OpenType face, or the PostScript name of a Standard 14 font.

Font.text_length.note: Measures with the shaping that drawing uses, including kerning; language=, script=, wmode=, and small_caps= are not available, and a line break raises.

Font.this.note: Handle of pymupdf's MuPDF binding; it has no PDF-level meaning.

Point.note: Immutable NamedTuple with finite coordinates, geometric operators, and tuple indexing, equality, and hashing.

Point.__setitem__.hint: Point values are immutable; build a new Point instead.

Point.transform.hint: Use p * m, which returns a new Point.

Rect.note: Immutable NamedTuple with finite coordinates, pymupdf's geometric operators, and tuple indexing, equality, and hashing.

Rect.__setitem__.hint: Rect values are immutable; build a new Rect instead.

Rect.include_point.hint: Use r | p, which returns a new Rect.

Rect.include_rect.hint: Use r | other, which returns a new Rect.

Rect.intersect.hint: Use r & other, which returns a new Rect.

Rect.normalize.hint: Use r.normalized(), which returns a new Rect.
Rect.normalize.note: No operator normalizes a rectangle, so the replacement needs a name.

Rect.transform.hint: Use r * m, which returns a new Rect.

IRect.note: Immutable NamedTuple of integers; fractional edges round outward.

IRect.__setitem__.hint: IRect values are immutable; build a new IRect instead.

IRect.include_point.hint: Use r | p, which returns a new IRect.
IRect.include_point.note: pymupdf's IRect version already returns a new IRect.

IRect.include_rect.hint: Use r | other, which returns a new IRect.
IRect.include_rect.note: pymupdf's IRect version already returns a new IRect.

IRect.intersect.hint: Use r & other, which returns a new IRect.

IRect.normalize.hint: Use r.normalized(), which returns a new IRect.
IRect.normalize.note: No operator normalizes a rectangle, so the replacement needs a name.

IRect.transform.hint: Use r * m, which returns a new IRect.

Quad.__setitem__.hint: Quad values are immutable; build a new Quad instead.

Quad.transform.hint: Use q * m, which returns a new Quad.

Matrix.note: Immutable NamedTuple with finite coordinates, geometric operators, and tuple indexing, equality, and hashing.

Matrix.__setitem__.hint: Matrix values are immutable; build a new Matrix instead.

Matrix.concat.hint: Use one * two, which returns a new Matrix.

Matrix.prerotate.hint: Use pylopdf.Matrix(deg) * m, which returns a new Matrix.

Matrix.prescale.hint: Use pylopdf.Matrix(sx, sy) * m, which returns a new Matrix.

Matrix.preshear.hint: Use pylopdf.Matrix(h, v, 1) * m, which returns a new Matrix.

Matrix.pretranslate.hint: Use pylopdf.Matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, tx, ty) * m, which returns a new Matrix.
